endCard.text: PART 3 — Follow so you don't miss it.
endCard.title: THE VILLAGE THAT REPEATS

narration.text: I spun around. Nobody. Just the bell, still ringing wrong, like it was laughing at me.

sentences.text: Just the bell, still ringing wrong, like it was laughing at me.

narration.text: Then, Tuesday. Bed. Bell. Bread. The old man and his goat. Same as always.

sentences.text: The old man and his goat.

narration.text: Except one thing. The chalk clock on my door didn't say three oh seven anymore. It said three oh eight.

sentences.text: The chalk clock on my door didn't say three oh seven anymore.

narration.text: One minute. After four hundred and twelve days, time had moved. One. Single. Minute. Somewhere, a clock was ticking that had never ticked before.

sentences.text: After four hundred and twelve days, time had moved.
Somewhere, a clock was ticking that had never ticked before.

narration.text: So I tested the rules. Before the baker could drop his tray, I knocked it out of his hands.

sentences.text: Before the baker could drop his tray, I knocked it out of his hands.

narration.text: The square went silent. And every single person turned to look at me. At the exact same time.

sentences.text: And every single person turned to look at me.

narration.text: Then they smiled. All of them. And went right back to what they were doing, like nothing happened.

sentences.text: And went right back to what they were doing, like nothing happened.

narration.text: The baker even picked up his bread, and said, lovely morning, Wren. He has never once said my name.

sentences.text: The baker even picked up his bread, and said, lovely morning, Wren.
He has never once said my name.

narration.text: So I followed the one thing that never leaves. The stranger's cart. It rolls in at seven fourteen, every single day. It never, ever rolls out.

sentences.text: So I followed the one thing that never leaves.
It rolls in at seven fourteen, every single day.

narration.text: It rolled behind the mill. And it didn't come out the other side. No tracks. No wheels. No stranger.

sentences.text: And it didn't come out the other side.
No tracks. No wheels. No stranger.

narration.text: Where it should have been, there was a trapdoor. I've walked past that spot a thousand times. It was never there before.

sentences.text: Where it should have been, there was a trapdoor.
I've walked past that spot a thousand times.

narration.text: Then the sun started moving. Fast. Like someone was dragging the day toward night. So I opened it.

sentences.text: Like someone was dragging the day toward night.

narration.text: Underneath were clocks. Hundreds of them. Chalked on every wall, in my handwriting. Some so old the chalk had almost faded away.

sentences.text: Chalked on every wall, in my handwriting.
Some so old the chalk had almost faded away.

narration.text: I counted them. Four hundred and twelve. One for every Tuesday. Every single one was crossed out. Except the last. Three oh eight. And under it, one word. Tomorrow.

sentences.text: Every single one was crossed out.

narration.text: Then the whisper came back. Right behind me. You always get this far, Wren. You always forget why. It pulled back its hood... and I knew that face. I see it every morning, in the mirror.

sentences.text: You always get this far, Wren.
I see it every morning, in the mirror.
